summary.headline: K.P. Energy Q2 FY27 total income rose about 78% YoY to Rs 540 crore, but margin compressed to about 12% and management guides it to persist for 2-4 quarters.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income for Q2 FY27 was about Rs 540 crore versus Rs 303 crore in Q2 FY26, with development (EPC) revenue at about Rs 527 crore. Profit after tax was Rs 26.92 crore, up slightly from Rs 26.08 crore in Q1 FY27, but H1 PAT fell to Rs 53.22 crore from Rs 61.37 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to labour cost and idling, right-of-way delays, crane availability, and raw material costs, and said margins would stay at current levels for 2 to 4 quarters. The order book stood at about 1.64 GW worth about Rs 1,940 crore as on 30 September 2026.

segments.name: EPC / development
segments.commentary: Revenue about Rs 527 crore in Q2 FY27 vs Rs 289 crore a year ago, about 82% growth, and now the main business. Order book about 1.64 GW worth about Rs 1,940 crore.

segments.name: IPP (own generation)
segments.commentary: Operational capacity 48.5 MW with 202 MW under development. Q2 FY27 generation about 2.75 crore units; H1 about 5.92 crore units. Power sale revenue about Rs 8.41 crore, down from Rs 10.01 crore.

guidance_outlook: Margins expected to stay around current levels (about 12% per analyst question, management did not dispute) for the next 2 to 4 quarters, citing ROW, labour, crane and raw material pressures.
Management said margin will not improve from 12% to 15% in the next four quarters; focus is on volume and turnover.
Around 1 GW of tenders under bidding; management assumed about 70% conversion (about 700 MW), valued at about Rs 7,000-8,000 crore, with results expected in 3 to 6 months.
No large new IPP capex planned beyond the 202 MW under development; company has guided that debt-to-equity will not exceed 2x.
Group-related BOP contracts to continue at arm's length, with the company moving to pure EPC scope going forward.
capex_capacity: IPP operational capacity 48.5 MW; 202 MW under development.
No significant further IPP capex planned, per management; debt-to-equity cap of 2x stated.
Indian wind turbine manufacturing capacity about 24 GW with 70-80% localisation, per management's industry commentary.
demand_pricing: Order book about 1.64 GW, about Rs 1,940 crore, as on 30 September 2026.
Management said margin compression reflects project mix, ROW rate increases, labour volatility, idle labour, crane availability and raw material costs; turbine supply carries a small markup.
Group-entity share of revenue about 50% in Q2 FY27, down from about 80-85% in Q1 FY27 per management.
India added about 3 GW of wind in H1 FY27; MNRE expects 7.5-8 GW in FY27. Management cites a 100 GW by 2030 target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profit decline YoY and what is the outlook? Are these one-off quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are now structurally lower as an EPC player, citing geopolitical conditions and market response; it expects margins to persist and points to about 1 GW of tenders under bidding.

qa_highlights.question: Is 12% a new normal margin, or will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should be assumed to stay at this level for now and that growth and scale will drive absolute profit.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving margins down: turbine pass-through, group-company pricing, or cost overruns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied lower pricing on group work (at arm's length, in line with market), attributed the change to project scope mix, and said large scale brings lower margins; group share of revenue about 50% in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What are the specific cost drivers behind the margin drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited labour volatility and idling, ROW delays across multiple locations, crane availability and raw material costs; no quantified cost split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin guidance change from 18-20% (May) to about 12% (August) and now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 average margin was about 21%, that the May guidance did not fully capture prolonged geopolitical effects, and that it will guide only on what it can see; it offered a one-on-one follow-up for the shareholder.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the MoU with a Saudi-based group company and whether the deadline will be extended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said talks are ongoing, it is taking longer, and there is nothing to disclose yet; it declined to comment on an extension.

risks_watch: Margin compression to about 12% (from about 21% FY26 average) with management guiding persistence for 2-4 quarters.
Related-party dependence: group entities were about 50% of Q2 revenue (vs 80-85% in Q1), with arm's-length pricing asserted but not quantified.
Inventory of Rs 1,067 crore (down from Rs 1,330 crore) and working capital intensity.

Change of statutory auditor to MSKC & Associates LLP from Mark & Associates; first quarter under new auditor delayed results call timing, with the gap between results and call flagged as a governance concern.
Pipeline conversion risk: about 70% assumed on about 1 GW of tenders, not yet awarded.
Sale of power revenue fell YoY to Rs 8.41 crore; H1 PBT down YoY despite revenue doubling.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and industry demand, but defensive and cautious on margins; management attributed compression to external factors and gave a near-term margin outlook but declined to make firm forward profit commitments. Evasive on group-company share, Saudi MoU status and the timing of the next results.
